vignette: John, a 48-year-old man of Oceania ethnicity, works as a roofer and is married to his high school sweetheart, Sarah. John's life took an unexpected turn on what was otherwise an ordinary Wednesday evening. He had just finished a long day at work and was heading home when he received a call from a former coworker, inviting him for drinks at a local bar. John accepted the invitation and met up with his old friend. Over several rounds of drinks, they reminisced about their time together on construction sites. As the evening wore on, John became increasingly uncomfortable as his friend's behavior grew more flirtatious and aggressive. Eventually, John found himself in an isolated alleyway behind the bar where his coworker forcibly assaulted him. The trauma of that night has haunted John ever since. He often wakes up in a cold sweat, drenched with fear as he relives those moments from the alley. His mind races through scenarios where he could have fought back or avoided the situation entirely. At work, the sound of rustling tar paper sends him into a panic; it reminds him too much of the night he was attacked. John's marriage has suffered due to his struggle with intimacy. He finds himself withdrawing from Sarah, often making excuses for why they shouldn't be physical. When she reaches out to comfort him, John becomes agitated and pushes her away, leaving both of them feeling hurt and confused. In the evenings, when he's alone, John tries to keep busy by working on crossword puzzles or watching television, anything to distract himself from the memories that haunt him. However, even these activities can trigger sudden bouts of anxiety. A news story about a similar incident will send his heart racing as he relives his own assault. His occupation as a roofer has become a source of both comfort and distress. The physical labor provides a sense of grounding and routine, but the isolation on construction sites often leaves him feeling vulnerable and exposed. He finds himself constantly scanning for potential threats and reacting sharply to sudden movements or sounds, leading to strained interactions with his coworkers. John's nights are filled with fragmented sleep and recurring nightmares where he relives the assault in vivid detail. The dreams leave him exhausted during the day, making it difficult for him to concentrate on his work. He has started to avoid social situations altogether, preferring the solitude of his home or the anonymity of working alone on a job site. Sarah, sensing her husband's distress, tries to offer support, but John often responds with anger and frustration, pushing her away even further. The tension between them is palpable, and Sarah feels helpless in trying to connect with him without triggering another episode of anxiety. Despite these challenges, John continues to work diligently, finding solace in the physicality and structure that his job provides. Yet, he remains haunted by the memory of that night, a constant reminder that he can never fully escape the trauma that has become an integral part of his life. In therapy sessions, John struggles to articulate his feelings but gradually opens up about his fears and guilt. He acknowledges that the assault continues to impact every aspect of his life, from his work performance to his relationship with Sarah. While he is determined to find a way forward, the weight of his past trauma makes it difficult for him to envision a future where he feels truly safe or at peace. Through their conversations, John begins to see that healing will be a long and challenging process, one that requires confronting the memories and fears that have kept him trapped in a cycle of anxiety and avoidance. Despite the obstacles ahead, there is a glimmer of hope as he starts to explore ways to cope with his trauma and rebuild connections with those around him.
